Haploid vs Diploid Cells
Cells that have 2 sets of chromosomes are diploid 
2 autosomes for each homologous pairs
2 sex chromosomes 
All human cells are diploid 
Except reproductive cells (sperm/egg) 
Diploid abbreviated as 2n
Human diploid (2n) number = 46
2 x 22 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes
explanation: Cells that contain two complete sets of chromosomes are described as diploid. In diploid cells, there are two autosomes for each homologous pair and two sex chromosomes. Diploid cells are abbreviated as 2n. Almost all cells in the human body are diploid, except for reproductive cells (gametes like sperm and egg cells). The human diploid (2n) number is 46, consisting of 44 autosomes (2 x 22 pairs) and 2 sex chromosomes.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation '2n' represent, and what is the 2n number for humans?
questions.exp: Diploid is abbreviated as 2n, and the human diploid (2n) number is 46.
